title: What Is Local Search? A Guide for Small Businesses
summary: Learn how local search works and discover SEO tips and strategies to help your small business rank higher, get found, and attract more customers.
body_markdown:
Key Takeaways


##


1. Local search is how nearby customers find businesses like yours; local SEO is how you improve your chances of appearing in those results.
2. Google primarily considers relevance, distance and prominence when determining which businesses appear in local search results.
3. Accurate business information and a strong online reputation make it easier for customers to find your business and feel confident choosing it.
4. “Near me,” conversational and AI-powered searches are changing how people discover local businesses, but they build on many of the same local-search fundamentals.
5. Measure success by more than rankings. Calls, website visits, direction requests and leads show whether greater visibility is translating into customer action.


## How Does Local Search Work?


Local search starts with intent. When someone searches, Google reads the query and decides whether they’re looking for something nearby. That signal, called local intent, comes through in a few ways.


Here’s how it’s different from local SEO:


**Local Search vs Local SEO**


**Local Search** **Local SEO**


**What it is** How customers find nearby businesses, products and services The steps a business takes to improve its visibility in local search results


**Example** A customer searches “plumber near me” A plumber optimizes its Google Business Profile, website, listings and reviews


**Goal** Find the right nearby business Make your business easier for nearby customers to find and choose


Local searches can signal location in a few different ways. Sometimes the location is explicit. Someone searches “plumber in Nashville” or “coffee shop near me.” The intent is obvious, so Google returns nearby options.


Other times Google infers it. Search “emergency plumber,” and you won’t type your[local city](https://www.thryv.com/blog/local-city-seo/) , but Google knows you want someone close who can come now. It pulls your location and shows local results even though you never named a place.


Once Google reads local intent, your business can appear across local search results in a few spots:


- **Google Maps:** the map view customers use to find and navigate to nearby businesses.
- **The Local Pack (also called Google local packs):** a prominent group of local business listings, typically accompanied by a map, that appears for many searches with local intent.
- **Organic results:** the standard blue-link web results below the pack, where your website and service pages compete.


Which businesses show up and in what order come down to three factors Google weighs.


### Relevance


Relevance is how well your business matches what the customer wants. A search for “gluten-free bakery” should surface a bakery that actually lists gluten-free products, not a general one. Complete, accurate listings and clear service pages help Google understand what you offer.


### Distance


Distance is how close you are to the searcher, or to the location in their search. You can’t move your shop, but accurate address, ZIP code, and service-area information ensure Google measures the distance correctly.


### Prominence


Prominence is how well-known and trusted your business is. Reviews, ratings, mentions across industry-specific directories, and a consistent presence online all tell Google you’re an established, credible choice.


You can’t control how close a searcher is to your business, but you can take steps to strengthen your relevance and prominence.

## The Transformative Impact of Local Search on Small Businesses


Local search connects you with customers at the exact moment they want what you sell. Someone searching “electrician near me,” for example, has a problem and is ready to hire. Show up, and you’re in the running.


That readiness turns into money fast. According to research,[93% of consumers](https://www.brightlocal.com/research/local-consumer-review-survey/) have purchased after reading customer reviews, and 27% have spent over $1,000. For many searches, the gap between discovery and purchase is a single afternoon.


Strong local visibility drives the actions that grow your business:


- **Calls and direction requests.** Inaccurate business listings, whether wrong hours, an outdated phone number, or incorrect categories, send customers to a competitor, since[53% of consumers](https://www.rioseo.com/resources/white-paper/2025-local-search-consumer-behavior-study/) won’t visit a business with incorrect or missing listing information.
- **Website visits.**[72% of consumers](https://www.rioseo.com/resources/white-paper/2025-local-search-consumer-behavior-study/) look for a business’s website during local search, and 54% visit it after reading positive reviews. A current, easy-to-navigate site turns that click into a booking.
- **Leads and new customers.**[85% of consumers](https://www.brightlocal.com/research/local-consumer-review-survey/) are more likely to use a business after reading positive reviews. Consistent visibility across Google, Bing Places, Maps, and directories keeps you in front of buyers at the moment they choose.


Local search also gives small businesses meaningful ways to compete for visibility. Keeping business information accurate, earning recent customer reviews and maintaining a complete online presence can help a smaller business stand out when nearby customers are deciding who to contact.

## What Influences Local Search Rankings?


Google says local search results are primarily based on three factors: relevance, distance and prominence. While you can’t control every factor — including how close a customer is to your business — there are several ways to help Google better understand your business and strengthen your local presence.


**Local Ranking Factors**


**Factor** **Why It Matters**


**Proximity to the searcher** Google ranks partly on how close you are to the searcher or the location they name. Keep your address, service-area settings, and map pin accurate.


**Google Business Profile and listings** Claim and verify your Google Business Profile, then keep your business name, description, address, phone number, hours, photos and services accurate and current. Complete information helps Google understand your business and helps customers know what to expect.


**Category accuracy** Choose the primary Google Business Profile category that most accurately reflects your core business, then add relevant secondary categories for additional services. Accurate categories help Google understand when your business is relevant to a local search.


**Reviews and reputation** Customer reviews help people evaluate your business and can support your prominence in Google local search. Focus on earning a steady flow of authentic reviews and responding to customer feedback. Reviews on other relevant platforms can also strengthen your broader online reputation.


**On-page and structured content** Clear service and location pages help search engines understand what you offer and where you operate. Helpful FAQs and relevant structured data can provide additional context about your business.


**Website authority and quality** A useful, technically sound website supports your visibility in traditional organic search. Create relevant local content, make your site easy to use on mobile devices, and earn credible links and mentions from other websites.


**Citations and directories** Keep your business information consistent across major maps, directories and relevant industry sites. Consistent listings make it easier for customers and search platforms to find accurate information about your business.


## “Near Me” & Conversational Searches


[“Near me” searches](https://www.thryv.com/blog/near-me-search-local-seo-opportunities/) signal strong local intent and often come from customers looking for a nearby option they can act on quickly. They rely on the same local-search fundamentals covered earlier, which makes accurate business information, relevance, and a strong online presence especially important.


What’s shifting is how people phrase these searches. They used to type short keywords. Now they ask full, specific questions, especially through voice queries:


- Instead of “plumber Nashville,” they ask “who can fix a burst pipe near me tonight.”
- Instead of “dentist,” they ask “which dentist near me takes new patients this week.”
- Instead of “Mexican restaurant,” they ask “best taco spot open now near me.”


Each of these carries details like urgency, timing, availability, and a specific need. To surface them, your business information has to answer those details directly.


Here’s how a small business turns that into practice:


- **Match the language customers use.** List services the way customers actually search for them.
- **Answer availability questions.** Update hours, including holidays, so you show up for “open now” searches.
- **Build plain-spoken service and location pages.** Write each page around the question a customer would ask.
- **Encourage authentic customer reviews.** A steady flow of recent feedback helps prospective customers understand the experiences others have had with your business.


The fundamentals don’t change for “near me” and conversational searches: make it clear what you offer, where you operate, and how customers can reach you. Writing the way customers talk is one more way to be the business they find.

## How AI Is Changing Local Search


Local search still works the way it always has at its core: Customers look for nearby businesses, and Google uses factors such as relevance, distance, and prominence to determine which businesses appear.


What’s changing is how customers search and where they discover local businesses. In addition to Google Search and Maps, customers can now ask[AI-powered search](https://www.thryv.com/blog/what-is-ai-search/) tools, conversational assistants and voice assistants for recommendations:


- **AI-powered search experiences.** Google’s AI Overviews and similar features read multiple sources, then summarize an answer at the top of the page. 60% of consumers click through at least sometimes after seeing one for a local business.
- **Conversational search.** Tools like ChatGPT let people ask full questions and get a short list of recommendations back. Use of these tools for local recommendations jumped from[6% to 45% in a single year](https://www.brightlocal.com/research/local-consumer-review-survey/) .
- **Voice assistants.** Siri (backed by Apple Intelligence), Alexa, and Google Assistant answer spoken “near me” questions, often reading back just one or two options.
- **Other major platforms.** Apple Maps, social platforms, and video sites increasingly surface local businesses based on reviews and engagement.


These searches tend to be more conversational and specific, often incorporating details such as urgency, availability, location or customer preferences.


For small businesses, that makes clear and trustworthy information even more important. Clear information about what your business offers and where you operate can make it easier for search platforms to understand when your business is a relevant option.


AI-powered discovery does not replace traditional local search. Instead, it adds new ways for customers to find and evaluate nearby businesses — often using many of the same signals that already support a strong local presence. That’s also why[SEO, AEO and GEO](https://www.thryv.com/blog/seo-vs-aeo-vs-geo-why-its-all-still-seo/) increasingly work together as part of a broader search visibility strategy.


### Practical Ways to Stand Out in AI-Driven Local Search


You don’t need a completely separate strategy for AI-powered local search. Start by strengthening the information and trust signals that make your business easier for both customers and search platforms to understand. The goal is not to optimize for AI instead of local search. It is to build a strong, consistent local presence that makes your business easier to find and understand wherever customers choose to search.


**How to Strengthen Your Visibility in AI-Driven Local Search**


The Priority How to Put It Into Practice


Keep your business information accurate and consistent. Make sure your business name, address, phone number, hours, service areas and services match across your website, Google Business Profile and other major platforms.


Answer the questions customers actually ask. Use clear service pages, location pages and FAQs to explain what you offer, where you operate and common questions about availability, pricing, services or next steps.


Build a strong and current reputation. Continue earning authentic customer reviews and responding to feedback. Recent reviews can help customers evaluate your business and strengthen the trust signals associated with your brand.


Make important answers easy to find. Don’t bury essential information. Make services, locations, availability and common customer questions easy to identify on your website. If your current site makes those updates difficult, a[small business website builder](https://www.thryv.com/features/professional-website/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=organicsocial) can make it easier to keep important information current.


## Where Should Small Businesses Start With Local Search?


If your local search presence needs work, you don’t have to fix everything at once. Start with the issues most likely to prevent customers from finding or choosing your business.


First, fix anything that could send a customer in the wrong direction. Check that your Google Business Profile is claimed and that your hours, phone number, address and service areas are correct.[Business listings management software](https://www.thryv.com/features/local-listings/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=organicsocial) can make it easier to keep those details consistent across the other places customers may find you online.


Next, look at what customers see when they find you. Is it immediately clear what you do? Do you have recent reviews? Can someone quickly tell whether you serve their area or offer the service they need? If keeping up with reviews becomes difficult,[small business reputation management software](https://www.thryv.com/features/reputation-management/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=organicsocial) can help make that work easier to manage. Your search visibility matters more when the information customers find gives them a reason to choose you.


Then build from there. Strengthen the service and location content on your website, including pages that support[local city SEO](https://www.thryv.com/blog/local-city-seo/) when you serve multiple cities or neighborhoods. Keep earning customer reviews and watch which local searches are driving calls, website visits, and bookings.


Start by removing the biggest barriers to getting found, then keep strengthening the signals that help customers find and trust your business over time.

## How to Measure Local Search Performance


You don’t need a complicated analytics setup to understand whether local search is working. A handful of metrics can show whether your visibility is improving and whether customers are taking action. Many are already available through your Google Business Profile.


Ask one question: are more people finding you, and are they taking action? Track these signals over time and watch the trend.


**Local Search Performance Metrics**


**What to Track** **What It Tells You** **Where to Find It**


**Profile views** How often people see your business in Search and Maps Google Business Profile


**Calls** How many customers call directly from your listing Google Business Profile


**Direction requests** How many people ask for directions to your location Google Business Profile


**Website clicks** How many searchers visit your site from your listing Google Business Profile


**Local keyword visibility** Whether you show up for the searches that matter Google Search Console or your SEO platform


**Reviews and rating** Whether your reputation is growing and staying fresh Google, Yelp, and other review sites


**Leads and bookings** How much of this activity turns into real business Your booking system, forms, or call tracking


A few tips to keep measurement useful:


- **Check monthly, not daily.** Local search results move gradually, so a month-over-month view shows how you’re progressing.
- **Prioritize customer actions.** Calls, direction requests and website clicks tell you more about customer intent than profile views alone.
- **Connect activity to outcomes.** If calls are up but bookings aren’t, look at how you’re handling those calls.
- **Track reviews as a metric.** A steady flow of recent, positive reviews is one of the clearest signs your local presence is healthy.


If your profile views are climbing and more of them turn into calls, directions, and bookings, your local search strategy is doing its job.
